trajectory_summary: This call has almost no rapport-building or objection-handling arc — it is a mechanical, checklist-driven intake of a pre-warmed, self-motivated lead who is calling back a missed call. The rep executes the qualification sequence (address, roof, title, utility, bill, credit) cleanly and books an appointment, but she never firmly establishes company identity, never pivots when the customer struggles for nearly five minutes with the bill portal, and never uses the customer's own stated bill-pain moment as leverage. The call ends in a booked appointment, which is the correct outcome given the customer's evident pre-existing intent, but several efficiency and legitimacy gaps would have mattered more had this customer been colder.

observed_outcome.quote: But I have you on the schedule at one tomorrow at 02:30
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (tomorrow) and time (2:30) are locked for an in-person appointment; the rep explicitly asked 'are you and your wife typically available in the mornings, afternoons, or evenings' at 14:27, which directly includes the co-owner wife in the scheduling question even though her individual confirmation isn't separately voiced back by the customer.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captures the monthly bill figure and moves directly into the credit qualifier without reflecting the number back as motivation or leverage; the flip should have landed right after 07:06, e.g. tying the $255 figure to the value of the upcoming appointment.

interest_reason_audit.reason_quote: Mhmm. And I'm planning to have a solar system at my place.
interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The customer volunteers his intent to get solar unprompted before the rep ever asks an interest question, and the rep never explicitly asks 'what interested you in solar' at any point in the call, so there was no dedicated moment to reinforce beyond the customer's initial volunteered statement.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Pivot to verbal bill read-back on tech friction
primary_coaching_focus.quote: Go so so because the Internet doesn't work well.
primary_coaching_focus.why: Nearly five minutes (08:34 to past 13:00) were spent waiting through a struggling portal login instead of pivoting to a verbal kWh read-back, which the schema specifically calls for within a 2-minute window — this is the single largest time-efficiency gap on the call and a directly correctable habit.

key_moments.quote: Hi. This is Elle with IIM Solar.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is an inbound callback-transfer scenario the schema doesn't explicitly define an intro template for (neither intros.standard nor intros.tesla covers a warm-transferred callback) — but even accounting for that gap, the rep never states a state, lead source, or any credibility anchor beyond a company name, and the company name itself is unclear in the audio. The downstream confusion at 14:59 and 15:44 traces directly back to this thin opening.

key_moments.quote: Alright. And then what was the number on that account?
key_moments.stewart_read: The very first substantive line of the call is a CRM lookup question, not a human greeting or acknowledgment of the customer's stated interest. There is no rapport beat before qualification begins.

key_moments.quote: Go so so because the Internet doesn't work well.
key_moments.stewart_read: From roughly 08:34 to past 13:00 — nearly five minutes — the customer struggles to log into his utility portal over poor internet. The schema's own protocol calls for pivoting to a verbal read-back within about 2 minutes of friction; instead the rep waits passively through repeated silences ('Okay,' 'Alright,' 'Yes.') without offering to have him read numbers aloud or defer bill collection to the specialist.

key_moments.quote: Give me a second. I I need I need to answer this.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer steps away for an unrelated call and the line goes dead for close to 100 seconds (03:07 to 04:54). The rep does not attempt to re-engage, check in, or say anything until the customer returns on his own — a passive hold with no call-control move from the rep.
